newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate closes up from low prior close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate closes up from low prior close.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates rates closed up 215 basis points on Friday at 19.40 percent due to what traders said was a return towards average trading levels after a low close on Thursday.
Traders also drew attention to the fact that overnight rates on bank paper actually closed below government paper, as opposed to the premium they normally offer.
"Bank paper is in great demand and there is a glut of government paper in the market, which is why the situation is so odd," a trader said.
Overnight rates on bank paper closed down 80 basis points at 18.80 percent.

Banco de Mexico drained 3.276 billion pesos from the system through a combination of three direct Cetes sales, which it assigned at 22.00-24.14 percent, and six repos which it placed at 18.63-20.89 percent.
June contracts fell 32 centavos to 77.68 pesos on Cetes futures trading on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.

Liquidity of 1.989 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system on Monday from prior central bank participation. Nonetheless, tax payments of about one billion pesos by state oil corporation Pemex were expected to reduce the ensuing liquidity surplus.
